Equinix stock: Record bookings support a third 2026 outlook raise
sum: Equinix strengthened its growth case after reporting record third-quarter bookings and raising its 2026 outlook for the third consecutive quarter. The update followed results for the period ended September 30, 2026, released on October 28 in the company's third-quarter results release.

Annualized gross bookings reached 533 million US dollars, an increase of 35 percent from a year earlier. Third-quarter revenue rose 11 percent to 2.571 billion US dollars on an as-reported basis, while normalized and constant-currency growth was 12 percent.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 15 percent to 1.321 billion US dollars. Adjusted funds from operations rose 20 percent to 1.156 billion US dollars, while AFFO per diluted share reached 11.64 US dollars on a reported basis. Equinix said a non-recurring fee related to its atNorth investment supported that comparison.

Chief Executive Adaire Fox-Martin said Equinix was accelerating capacity delivery to meet broad-based demand. The company introduced Fabric One for distributed cloud, network and AI environments and announced Equinix Inference Exchange with NVIDIA and Together AI.

Nearly 40 percent more cabinets are planned for delivery in 2026 than initially expected. For the full year, Equinix expects revenue of 10.325 billion to 10.365 billion US dollars, adjusted EBITDA of 5.290 billion to 5.330 billion US dollars and AFFO of 4.340 billion to 4.380 billion US dollars. Fourth-quarter revenue is forecast at 2.684 billion to 2.724 billion US dollars, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 49 to 50 percent.

Equinix stock: Record bookings support third outlook raise
sum: Equinix reported record demand and raised its full-year outlook again after the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. In its October 28 results release, the data center operator reported annualized gross bookings of 533 million US dollars, up 35 percent from a year earlier.

Third-quarter revenue rose 11 percent year over year on an as-reported basis to 2.571 billion US dollars. On a normalized and constant-currency basis, revenue increased 12 percent. Monthly recurring revenue grew at a double-digit rate for the fourth consecutive quarter, while interconnection revenue advanced 10 percent.

Adjusted EBITDA reached 1.321 billion US dollars, up 15 percent as reported and 14 percent on a normalized and constant-currency basis. Adjusted funds from operations rose 20 percent as reported to 1.156 billion US dollars. AFFO per diluted share increased 18 percent as reported to 11.64 US dollars, or 12 percent on a normalized basis excluding the benefit of a fee related to the atNorth joint venture.

Net income attributable to common stockholders rose 31 percent to 489 million US dollars, and diluted earnings per share increased 29 percent to 4.93 US dollars. The company said the net income comparison benefited partly from a non-recurring fee connected with its atNorth investment, making the normalized AFFO figures more relevant for assessing recurring operating momentum.

Chief Executive Adaire Fox-Martin said the company was accelerating capacity to meet broad-based demand. Equinix also introduced Fabric One, a connectivity service for distributed cloud, network and AI environments, and announced Equinix Inference Exchange with NVIDIA and Together AI. The company said nearly 40 percent more cabinets were planned for delivery in 2026 than initially expected.

For the fourth quarter, Equinix expects revenue of 2.684 billion to 2.724 billion US dollars and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 49 to 50 percent. For the full year, revenue guidance now stands at 10.325 billion to 10.365 billion US dollars, adjusted EBITDA at 5.290 billion to 5.330 billion US dollars and AFFO at 4.340 billion to 4.380 billion US dollars. The company expects full-year revenue growth of about 12 percent and AFFO per share growth of 11 to 12 percent on a normalized and constant-currency basis.

Equinix stock: Q3 growth drives a third 2026 guidance raise
sum: Equinix reported stronger third-quarter operations on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, and raised its full-year outlook for the third consecutive quarter. The company said demand remained broad across connectivity, data centers and artificial-intelligence workloads.

According to the Equinix investor release, third-quarter revenue increased 11 percent year over year to 2.571 billion US dollars. Normalized revenue growth at constant currency was 12 percent, while adjusted EBITDA rose 15 percent to 1.321 billion US dollars and the margin reached 51 percent.

Annualized gross bookings reached a record 533 million US dollars, up 35 percent from the prior year. Equinix added 6,900 net interconnections, while interconnection revenue rose 10 percent and Fabric revenue increased 24 percent.

Net income attributable to common stockholders rose 31 percent to 489 million US dollars, or 4.93 US dollars per diluted share. The result included a non-recurring fee related to the atNorth joint venture. Diluted AFFO per share increased 18 percent as reported and 12 percent on a normalized, constant-currency basis excluding that fee.

Equinix now expects 2026 revenue of 10.325 billion to 10.365 billion US dollars, compared with the previous range of 10.205 billion to 10.285 billion US dollars. Adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to 5.290 billion to 5.330 billion US dollars, while AFFO per share is expected at 43.71 to 44.11 US dollars.

For the fourth quarter, management expects revenue of 2.684 billion to 2.724 billion US dollars and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 49 to 50 percent. Total capital expenditures for 2026, excluding real-estate acquisitions and xScale, remain planned at 5 billion to 6 billion US dollars. Nearly 40 percent more cabinets than initially anticipated are scheduled for delivery in 2026, raising execution and funding requirements alongside the growth opportunity.

sum: - Equinix (NASDAQ:EQIX) Real Estate Equinix Inc (NASDAQ:EQIX) 993.69 USD -20.010 1.974% Last Updated at: 2026-11-02T21:00:00Z raised its full-year range and multi-year growth ambitions at its latest-quarter report.
- Equinix filed details on xScale ventures, capacity spending and note issuance in its quarterly report.
- Power availability and customer demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remain central to the Equinix story.

The most recent reference points are the latest-quarter results delivered at the end of July and the quarterly report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which together described rising revenue, a lifted full-year range and a sharply improved multi-year growth ambition, even though the quarter-ahead revenue range disappointed some market participants. Demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure, power availability and heavy capital spending are the main storylines surrounding the name.

At the end of July, Equinix reported latest-quarter revenue that came in above what the market had anticipated, and it raised its full-year revenue range along with its range for adjusted funds from operations per share. News reports noted that shares moved lower on the day because the revenue range given for the following quarter had a midpoint a little under expectations. That reaction illustrates how a stock can fall even on a beat and a raise.

Alongside the quarterly numbers, management raised its multi-year expectations. According to press coverage, the company now expects annual revenue growth in a higher band than before, running through the end of the decade, and a similarly upgraded range for growth in adjusted funds from operations per share. Such a revision signals management's belief that the demand cycle for digital infrastructure has strengthened.

Equinix to Post Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
sum: Equinix, Inc. EQIX is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 28, after market close. The company's quarterly results are likely to display a year-over-year rise in revenues and adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) per share.

In the previous quarter, this Redwood City, CA-based data center real estate investment trust (REIT) reported an AFFO of $10.78 per share, outpacing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $11.25. The results reflected higher recurring revenues on stronger underlying demand and robust bookings. Non-recurring revenues more than doubled, driven primarily by xScale leasing fees.

Over the preceding four quarters, EQIX's AFFO per share surpassed the consensus estimate on two occasions and missed in the remaining quarters, with the average beat being 2.05%. This is depicted in the graph below:

In the third quarter of 2026, Equinix is likely to have benefited from the solid demand for interconnected data center infrastructure. Enterprises' and service providers' continued efforts to integrate artificial intelligence into their strategies and offerings and advance their digital transformation agendas are likely to keep demand up in the upcoming years.

Moreover, the demand for Equinix's interconnected ecosystem is likely to have remained strong, driven by accelerating enterprise cloud adoption and increasing demand from cloud and internet customers for highly interconnected data center space.

The company's recurring revenue model, which comprises colocation, related interconnection and managed infrastructure services, is expected to have supported stable cash flows in the to-be-reported quarter, boosting the data center REIT's top line.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for colocation revenues is pegged at $1.81 billion, suggesting growth from $1.64 billion in the prior-year period. The consensus mark for interconnection revenues is pinned at $469.6 million, indicating growth from $422 million in the prior-year period.

CoreWeave Shares Sink After Bernstein Warns Of Slower AI Training
sum: CoreWeave CRWV shares fell 6% Monday as investors weighed the potential impact of slower artificial intelligence model training on data-center demand, according to a Monday investor note from Bernstein.
Analyst Maidson Rezaei said facilities in rural and Tier 3 markets could face greater pressure because many were developed around training workloads that are less sensitive to network latency.

Bernstein estimates about 70% of a 488-gigawatt U.S. data-center development pipeline is located in rural or Tier 3 areas. CoreWeave has about 25% of its active U.S. power and roughly 74% of contracted power in Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets.

The firm said CoreWeave's existing backlog is largely supported by take-or-pay agreements, which may limit near-term risk. However, demand for contracted capacity that has not yet been sold could weaken if training activity slows.

Equinix EQIX, Digital Realty Trust DLR and Csquare CSQR may be less exposed because most of their capacity is located in metropolitan markets. Bernstein rates CoreWeave Underperform with a $74 target, while assigning Outperform ratings to the other three.

Equinix Stock Has A Message For Management
sum: The company raised its outlook on booming AI demand, but the stock is telling a different story by standing still.

Back on Apr 29, 2026, Equinix (EQIX) management did what you want to see management do: they took a public victory lap. Citing a surge in AI-driven demand, the company raised its full-year revenue target to $10.19 Bil. The market’s reaction since? A shrug. The stock has returned a perfectly flat +0.05%, leaving investors with a simple, nagging question: If the AI story is this good, what’s the holdup?

Management certainly laid out a compelling case. Q1, they said, was the “largest quarter of total sales activity in our history,” with that activity up more than 35% year-over-year. The engine for this growth is clear: executives noted that “approximately 60% of our largest deals in Q1 were AI-related.” The work involves building the interconnected plumbing for the AI revolution, a more fundamental task than simply filling racks. The company’s high-margin interconnection services are booming, with bookings for its Fabric platform soaring 70% year-over-year. This is the story that powered the guidance raise and created a record backlog. Yet, the stock price suggests the market heard the story but is waiting for the punchline.

The market seems to be looking past the booming sales and focusing on the price tag. To meet this demand, Equinix is spending heavily. The company now expects total capital expenditures to hit the top end of its prior range at $4.1 billion for the year. That’s a massive outlay, and it brings the central tension for the stock into sharp focus. Investors have long prized Equinix for its high returns on capital. The fear, bubbling under the surface, is whether these new, power-hungry AI workloads require so much more expensive infrastructure that they will inevitably dilute the very profitability that made the stock a winner.

For their part, executives insist the discipline that got them here isn’t going anywhere. They are still underwriting new projects to deliver returns in the “mid-20s percent,” even with the higher-density requirements of AI. But the market is in a “show-me” state. It has seen the forecast and heard the promises.
